original_question: What necessary and sufficient conditions guarantee the existence of bi-orthogonal local coordinate systems on a Riemannian manifold, without assuming any affine connections a priori?
target_in_paper: Section 5 (Hiroshi Matsuzoe), item 1, first open problem under "Elucidate what geometric structures are essential to information geometry": "Give a necessary and sufficient condition for bi-coordinates to exist on a Riemannian manifold," with bi-orthogonality defined by Equation (1).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's main target very well: it is a local existence/characterization question on a Riemannian manifold, about bi-orthogonal coordinates, and it preserves the paper's emphasis that no affine connection should be assumed a priori.
missing_details: The paper defines the relevant coordinates explicitly: on a common local chart U, two coordinate systems x=(x^1,...,x^n) and y=(y_1,...,y_n) are bi-orthogonal when g(∂/∂x^i, ∂/∂y_j)=δ_i^j for all i,j=1,...,n.
The existence question is local, so a fully stand-alone formulation should state the quantifier: for every point p in M, one asks for such coordinates on some neighborhood U of p.
The ambient object should be stated explicitly as a smooth finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold (M,g).

The nearby context motivates the problem by noting that dually flat spaces admit bi-orthogonal coordinates whose coordinate systems are dual affine; including this motivation helps keep the scope aligned with the paper.
There are no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or "for all sufficiently large m" conditions in this problem; those kinds of data are simply not part of the paper's statement.
refined_question: Let (M,g) be a smooth n-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions for the following local property: for every point p in M, there exists a neighborhood U of p and two smooth local coordinate systems x=(x^1,...,x^n) and y=(y_1,...,y_n) on U such that g(∂/∂x^i, ∂/∂y_j)=δ_i^j on U for all i,j=1,...,n; that is, characterize exactly when a Riemannian manifold admits bi-orthogonal local coordinates in this sense, without assuming any affine connection a priori.
justification: In this paper, the exact match is not a numbered theorem or conjecture but an open problem in Section 5, item 1. After defining bi-orthogonal coordinates by Equation (1) and noting that dually flat spaces provide such coordinates as dual affine coordinates, Matsuzoe asks for a necessary and sufficient condition for bi-coordinates to exist on a Riemannian manifold. Your draft is therefore already close to the paper, but it is not fully stand-alone because it omits the explicit coordinate identity, the common-chart/local-around-each-point quantifier, and the notation for the two coordinate systems. The rewrite keeps the scope narrow and does not absorb the separate follow-up question in the paper about a generalized Pythagorean theorem without mutually dual affine connections.
